findings.title: Password form submits over HTTP
findings.description: A password-bearing form submits to cleartext HTTP.
findings.impact: Credentials may be exposed to interception.
findings.remediation: Use HTTPS-only authentication endpoints and redirect/block cleartext access.

findings.title: Session-like cookie missing HttpOnly
findings.description: Cookie `session_id` appears session/auth related but lacks HttpOnly.
findings.impact: Client-side script access can increase credential exposure in case of XSS.
findings.remediation: Add HttpOnly when JavaScript access is not required.

findings.title: CORS origin reflection detected
findings.description: The response reflected an arbitrary test Origin value in Access-Control-Allow-Origin.
findings.impact: Origin reflection can enable unintended cross-origin access when combined with sensitive resources or credentials.
findings.remediation: Use a strict allow-list and validate origins server-side rather than reflecting arbitrary Origin values.

findings.title: Sensitive-looking page lacks Cache-Control evidence
findings.description: A sensitive-looking URL does not expose a restrictive Cache-Control policy.
findings.impact: Shared/private caching could retain sensitive material depending on framework/proxy behavior.
findings.remediation: Review caching policy and explicitly control storage for authenticated/sensitive responses.
findings.evidence_summary: No Cache-Control header on sensitive-looking path.

findings.remediation: Disable introspection in production when it is not required, or restrict it to trusted development/admin contexts.

findings.title: CSRF protection not obvious in state-changing form
findings.description: No commonly named CSRF token field was observed. This is a review candidate, not proof of a CSRF flaw.
findings.impact: State-changing requests may require server-side CSRF defenses.
findings.remediation: Verify framework/token/header-based CSRF controls for state-changing operations.
findings.evidence_summary: No common CSRF token field name detected.
